findings: Prop. 10 (l.1122–1125) is imprecise at the interior facette. For a ∈ int W, the facette of a is always conical: W_a = S(n), the contingent is S(n), its noyau is S(n), and the facette's support is S(n). Then S(n)/L = S(E/E) is empty and has no convex body (Benzecri.interior_facette_conique). The printed proof's « il en est de même du contingent considéré comme partie de S(n)/L » (l.1127–1128) silently assumes L ≠ S(n). Every conical facette of support ≠ S(n) is covered with no further hypothesis (prop10_contingent_conique); whether the interior facette is the only one of support S(n) is not formalized. This is the edge case the dispatch anticipated (reading (a)), like OQ-165 (d).
questions: « s'identifie à un corps convexe de S(n)/L » (l.1124). Reading taken: the contingent C contains l = s(L − O) and corresponds to quotientImage L C under convexQuotientEquiv (Déf. 10 of Ch. 1). S(n)/L = S(E/L) is read as S(m) through a linear identification E/L ≃ ℝ^{m+1}. The statement is proved for every such identification, and one exists with m + 1 + dim L = n + 1.

findings: Déf. 6 (l.1134–1136) refers to « la définition 6 du paragraphe 2 », but the sum is § 2 Déf. 5 (l.548–558); Déf. 6 of § 2 is « distingué ». Read literally, that sense does not fit. § 2 Déf. 5 asks for a convex w with empty noyau (S(n) has noyau S(n)), and its two-summand form asks w to be the union of the open segments joining l to l′. Those segments miss l and l′. So S(n) is a sum of two linear subvarieties in that sense only in the degenerate splittings L = E, L′ = 0 and L = 0, L′ = E (Benzecri.Sphere.estSomme2_univ_linearSubvariety_iff). The printed bracket gives the intended notion, E = L ⊕ L′ (estSommeLineaire_iff). The dispatch's note « EstSomme2 for Déf. 6's somme de L et de L′ (L ⊕ L′ = E) » is mistaken for the same reason.
questions: Déf. 6's « somme … au sens de la définition 6 du paragraphe 2 ». Reading taken: the bracket « [L ∩ L′ = ∅, S(n) enveloppe convexe de L et L′] » (EstSommeLineaire ⇔ IsCompl L L′), not § 2's EstSomme2, which is degenerate here. Should the bracket be the definition of record? If so, the row can be marked.

instances: Conical facette and its base (Benzecri.FacetteConiqueInstance), on S(2), using the closed triangle T = FacetteDualeInstance.simplexS 2. T is a convex body (isCorpsConvexeS_simplexS). The contingent at its vertex s(e₀) is s({x₁ ≥ 0, x₂ ≥ 0}) (contingent_vertex0). Its noyau is {±s(e₀)} = supportK {s(e₀)} (noyau_contingent_vertex0, supportK_vertex0). So {s(e₀)} is a conical facette (isFacetteConique_vertex0), and Prop. 10's hypotheses hold there (prop10_instance). With L′ = {x₀ = 0} = span(e₁, e₂): IsCompl L0 L1 holds, and the base of the vertex in L′ is the opposite closed edge T ∩ L′ (isBaseFacetteConique_vertex0).

Non-conical facette: the closed round cap cap = s({x₀ ≥ 0, x₂ ≥ 0, x₁² ≤ x₀x₂}), a circular cone, is a convex body of S(2) (isCorpsConvexeS_cap). At its boundary point s(e₀), s(e₁) lies in the noyau of the contingent (mk_eB_mem_noyau, through the half-plane {a e₁ + b e₂, b > 0} ⊆ W_p). The support of the facette lies in the axis {x₁ = x₂ = 0} (facetteK_capPt_subset). So the facette of s(e₀) is not conical (cap_facette_example).

To show that an image in S(E/L) ≅ S(m) is a convex body, use isCorpsConvexeS_image_quotient. Go through φ = e ∘ mkQ: K + L = K makes φ(K)ᶜ = φ(Kᶜ), and LinearMap.isOpenMap_of_finiteDimensional gives closedness and interior. mapEquiv_image_ofCone moves ofCone across a linear equivalence.
